body.objective: Students will be able to balance within the ensemble pyramid.
body.iCan: I can balance within the ensemble pyramid.
successCriteria: I can balance my sound within the ensemble pyramid
I can blend with my section by matching tone, volume and pitch
I can play straight and swing eighths and hear the difference
body.hook: A band of 40 players can sound like one giant instrument or like 40 people playing at the same time. The difference is balance and blend: listening more than you play.

vocabulary.definition: The right volume relationship between parts so all are heard as intended.
When individual sounds merge so no single player sticks out.
A model where low instruments play with the most sound and high instruments with less.
How in tune a player is with others.
A feel where eighth notes are played long-short, like a triplet.

study.title: Building the Pyramid
study.question: How does a band balance and blend into one sound?
study.passage:
The ensemble pyramid: Imagine a pyramid. The base is wide: tubas, baritones, bass clarinets, bari saxes. The middle: horns, trombones, tenor saxes, clarinets. The top is narrow: flutes, trumpets, alto saxes. Low instruments carry more sound; high instruments sit on top. If the top is louder than the base, the band sounds thin and shrill.
Part 1, Build a chord (15 minutes): Play a B-flat concert chord. Basses start, then each section enters one at a time from the bottom up. Each section should be able to hear the section below it.
Part 2, Section blend (10 minutes): Each section plays a long tone. Rule: if you can hear yourself above your neighbour, play softer. Match the tone and start and end together.
Part 3, Intonation (10 minutes): Use a drone. Listen for "beats" (wobbles); adjust until they disappear.
Part 4, Straight vs swing (15 minutes): Play a B-flat scale in eighths, straight. Then swing it: long-short, like "doo-ba doo-ba," with the long note two thirds and the short note one third of the beat. Accent the off-beats lightly. Play a short jazz chart excerpt with swing feel.
study.source: Original rehearsal plan written for this lesson; the ensemble pyramid is a widely used band teaching model.
steps: Build a chord from the bottom up
Blend with your section on long tones
discussion: Why do low instruments need more sound than high ones?
What did you change to blend with your section?
How do you hear when you're out of tune?
How does swing change the feel of the same notes?
study.product: In a recorded rehearsal, demonstrate balance by building a chord and blend in a section long tone, then write a reflection on two adjustments you made.

examples.title: Pyramid
examples.problem: Flutes are louder than tubas in a chord. What happens?
examples.answer: The band sounds thin and shrill

examples.title: Blend
examples.problem: You can hear yourself clearly above the section. What should you do?
examples.answer: Play softer until you merge with your neighbours

examples.title: Swing ratio
examples.problem: In swing, how is a beat divided?
examples.answer: Long note two thirds, short note one third

examples.title: Intonation
examples.problem: You hear a wobble playing with a drone. What does it mean?
examples.answer: You're out of tune; adjust until the wobble stops
examples.explore: How do you know whether to go up or down?

practice.a: The right volume relationship between parts.
When sounds merge so no one sticks out.
How in tune a player is.
Eighths played long-short with a triplet feel.

practice.q: Which instruments form the base of the ensemble pyramid?
practice.a: Low brass and low woodwinds such as tubas and bari saxes.

practice.q: Why build a chord from the bottom up?
practice.a: So each section hears and balances on the one below.

practice.q: What is the blend rule for section playing?
practice.a: If you hear yourself above your neighbour, play softer.

practice.q: What do "beats" in a sound mean?
practice.a: The notes are out of tune.

practice.q: How is the beat divided in swing?
practice.a: Long two thirds, short one third.

practice.q: What should you match to blend?
practice.a: Volume, tone, pitch, and note starts and ends.

practice.q: Why does a top-heavy band sound thin?
practice.a: High instruments cover the warm low foundation.

practice.q: How do you decide whether to raise or lower your pitch?
practice.a: Adjust slightly; if the beats slow down you're moving the right way.

practice.q: How does swing change the style of a piece?
practice.a: It gives a relaxed, jazzy groove.

practice.q: Why is listening more important than playing loudly in ensembles?
practice.a: The goal is one combined sound, not individual volume.

misconceptions: Thinking playing louder is always better
Thinking tuning happens only at the start of rehearsal
exitTicket: Sketch the ensemble pyramid and label two instruments at each level.

test.title: Practice test: Balance within the ensemble pyramid

items.q: Balance means
options: A) the right volume relationship between parts
items.answer: A) the right volume relationship between parts

items.q: Blend is achieved when
options: D) no single player sticks out
items.answer: D) no single player sticks out

items.q: Swing eighths are played
items.answer: C) long-short

items.q: Intonation refers to
items.answer: A) playing in tune

items.q: The base of the ensemble pyramid includes
items.answer: D) tubas and baritones

items.q: When building a chord, sections enter
items.answer: B) from the bottom up

items.q: If you hear yourself above your section, you should
items.answer: C) play softer

items.q: A wobble when playing with a drone means
options: A) you are out of tune
B) you are perfectly in tune
items.answer: A) you are out of tune

items.q: In swing, the long note takes
options: A) two thirds of the beat
B) one quarter of the beat
items.answer: A) two thirds of the beat

items.q: A top-heavy band sounds
items.answer: A) thin and shrill

items.q: The best evidence that you are blending is
options: A) you hear the section, not yourself
items.answer: A) you hear the section, not yourself

items.q: Swing differs from straight eighths in
items.answer: D) rhythmic feel

items.q: Define blend.
items.answer: When individual sounds merge so no one sticks out.

items.q: What is intonation?
items.answer: How in tune a player is with others.

items.q: Describe the ensemble pyramid.
items.answer: Low instruments provide the most sound at the base; high instruments play less on top.

items.q: Explain how to blend with your section.
items.answer: Match volume, tone, pitch and articulation; play softer if you stick out.

items.q: Explain the difference between straight and swing eighths.
items.answer: Straight are even; swing are long-short with a triplet feel.

items.q: How do you tune using a drone?
items.answer: Listen for beats and adjust until they disappear.

items.q: Explain why low instruments carry more sound in a balanced band.
items.answer: They create the warm foundation the higher parts sit on.

items.q: Describe two adjustments you made in rehearsal to improve balance or blend.
items.answer: Answers vary.
